title: Cat and Mouse in Partnership
text:
A cat persuaded a mouse to set up house with her. To prepare for winter they bought a pot of fat, and after some thought they hid it in the safest place they knew: under the altar of the church, where nobody would dare take anything.

Before long the cat began to long for the fat. She told the mouse that a cousin had asked her to be godmother at a christening, and she went out. She went straight to the church and licked the top off the fat. When she came home, the mouse asked the baby's name. Top-off, said the cat.

Soon she was invited to another christening, she said, and this time she ate half the pot. The baby was called Half-done. The third time she finished it, and the name she gave was All-gone. The mouse thought these were very strange names, but she trusted her partner.

When winter came and food was scarce, the mouse suggested they go and fetch their store. They went to the church and found the pot empty. Suddenly the mouse understood everything, and she began to say so. The cat told her to be quiet or she would eat her too. But the words were already on the mouse's lips. The cat sprang on her, seized her and swallowed her.
lesson: Shared resources need shared oversight. If a partner's explanations keep getting stranger, check the store before it is gone and before you are the only one left trusting.
source: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmarchen, No. 2, Cat and Mouse in Partnership
